key_insight: Prompt caching can substantially reduce cost and latency for long-horizon, tool-using LLM agents, but naive caching strategies can degrade correctness—careful strategy selection and invalidation rules are required to keep caches both efficient and safe.
problem_solved: Quantifies and characterizes the costs, latency benefits, and correctness trade-offs of prompt caching in multi-turn, tool-heavy LLM agent workloads, where long contexts and frequent API calls make efficiency and cache consistency critical.
method: Empirical evaluation of prompt caching across representative long-horizon agentic tasks (many-turn tool use), measuring cost, latency, and task success rates as context length scales.
Comparison of caching strategies (e.g., full-prompt, prefix/partial, and semantics-aware caching) and analysis of cache invalidation/failure modes that cause correctness regressions.
Ablations and breakdowns showing where caching yields wins versus where it introduces errors, with guidelines for safe caching policies.
impact: Provides actionable evidence and best-practice guidance so ML engineers can reduce API cost and latency for agentic systems without unknowingly compromising correctness—enabling more scalable production deployment of tool-using LLM agents.
visual_elements: Bar chart: percent cost and latency reduction of different caching strategies across task horizons.
Line chart: task success rate vs. number of cached turns (shows where naive caching harms correctness).
Flow diagram: cache decision pipeline (when to reuse cached prompt vs. recompile full context) with invalidation triggers.
Heatmap or table of failure modes: types of tool/state changes that break cached prompts and recommended mitigations.
paper_title: Don't Break the Cache: An Evaluation of Prompt Caching for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
paper_authors: Elias Lumer, Faheem Nizar, Akshaya Jangiti, Kevin Frank, Anmol Gulati
